senses.definition: In stories, a power that makes impossible things happen.
senses.example: The wizard used magic to make the flowers glow.

senses.definition: A performance in which someone uses skill and tricks to make surprising things appear to happen.
senses.example: The party had music, games, and magic.

senses.definition: Hot, partly or fully melted rock beneath Earth’s surface.
senses.example: Magma collected below the volcano.

senses.definition: An object that can attract certain metals, such as iron, and pull or push other magnets without touching them.
senses.example: The magnet held our drawing against the refrigerator door.

senses.definition: The angle between the direction a compass points locally and the direction to Earth’s geographic north pole.
senses.example: A map showed the magnetic declination for the area so we could compare the needle with true north.

senses.definition: The area in which a magnet or moving electric charge can exert a magnetic force.
senses.example: A compass needle responds to Earth’s magnetic field.

senses.definition: The forces linked to magnets that can pull certain materials toward a magnet or make magnets push or pull each other.
senses.example: We used a compass to see one effect of magnetism.

senses.definition: To make something look bigger, often by using a lens.
senses.example: This hand lens can magnify a speck of sand.

senses.definition: To make something seem larger, stronger, or more serious.
senses.example: The silly rumor magnified a small problem until everyone was worried.

senses.definition: Letters or packages carried and delivered to people.
senses.example: There was a letter for me in the mail.

senses.definition: To send something through a service that delivers letters or packages.
senses.example: We mailed a card to our cousins.

senses.definition: More important, larger, or used more than the others.
senses.example: Turn left at the main entrance to the school.

senses.definition: Especially big or important.
senses.example: A major change to the plan was moving the picnic indoors.

senses.definition: A main subject someone studies in college.
senses.example: My cousin’s college major is history.

senses.definition: To create or put something together.
senses.example: We made a bird feeder from things we had at home.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to act, feel, or change in a certain way.
senses.example: The joke made me laugh.

senses.definition: To be clear enough to understand or to be reasonable.
senses.example: Drawing the route helped the directions make sense.

senses.definition: To do something that helps balance out a loss, mistake, or problem.
senses.example: We could start earlier tomorrow to make up for the time we lost today.

senses.definition: A building or large area with many stores next to one another.
senses.example: We went to the mall to buy a birthday card.

senses.definition: A kind of animal whose mothers feed their young milk. Mammals have hair at least at some stage in life.
senses.example: Dolphins and bears are both mammals.

senses.definition: To be in charge of how something is run.
senses.example: The coach manages the schedule for our team.

senses.definition: To succeed at something, often when it is difficult.
senses.example: We managed to fit the last puzzle piece into place.

senses.definition: A person who is in charge of running part or all of a business, team, or activity.
senses.example: The store manager helped us find the owner of the lost bag.

senses.definition: A family of games in which players move small counters one at a time among pits on a board.
senses.example: We learned a kind of mancala using seeds.

senses.definition: A way of doing something or behaving.
senses.example: The teacher spoke in a calm manner.

senses.definition: Rules or habits for acting politely, usually in the plural.
senses.example: Saying thank you is good manners.

senses.definition: A drawing or display that shows where places or things are.
senses.example: We used the trail map to find a picnic spot.

senses.definition: To draw or record where things are.
senses.example: The class mapped the trees on the playground.

senses.definition: The part of a map that explains what the colors, lines, and pictures on it stand for.
senses.example: We checked the map legend to learn which blue line showed a stream.

senses.definition: A guide that compares a distance on a map with a distance on the ground.
senses.example: The map scale shows that one mark on the ruler stands for one mile.

senses.definition: A tree whose leaves often have several pointed parts. Sap from some kinds can be turned into syrup.
senses.example: The maple outside school had bright orange leaves.

senses.definition: A small hard ball of glass or stone used in games.
senses.example: The green marble rolled into the ring.

senses.definition: A hard stone that can be polished and used in statues or buildings.
senses.example: The museum hallway had a floor made of marble.

senses.definition: To walk with regular, firm steps, often as part of a group.
senses.example: The band marched past the town hall.

senses.definition: An event where people walk together, often to support something or demand a change.
senses.example: Families joined a march to ask for safer streets.

senses.definition: A blank area between the edge of a page and the writing or picture.
senses.example: I wrote a short note in the margin.

senses.definition: The amount by which one result is higher or lower than another.
senses.example: Our team won by a margin of two points.

senses.definition: A spot, sign, or line that can be seen on something.
senses.example: The cup left a ring-shaped mark on the table.

senses.definition: To make a sign on something so it can be noticed or found later.
senses.example: Please mark the page with this slip of paper.

senses.definition: A written score that shows how well you did on schoolwork.
senses.example: Sana earned a good mark on her spelling quiz.

senses.definition: A place or event where people buy and sell things.
senses.example: We bought peaches at the market.

senses.definition: The people who are able or likely to buy a kind of thing.
senses.example: There is a market for warm gloves in places with cold winters.

senses.definition: To offer something for sale and tell people why they might want to buy it.
senses.example: The baking club marketed its muffins by putting signs around the school.

senses.definition: To become someone’s spouse, or to lead the ceremony where two people agree to do that.
senses.example: My aunt will marry her partner in July.

senses.definition: A kind of wetland where grasses or other soft-stemmed plants are common.
senses.example: We saw long-legged birds among the plants in the marsh.

senses.definition: A kind of mammal with young that are born at a very early stage and keep growing while they nurse. Many young marsupials develop inside a pouch on their mother.
senses.example: An opossum is a marsupial that carries its tiny babies in a pouch.

senses.definition: A covering for the face, worn for protection, as a costume, or to hide who you are.
senses.example: Our play had a fox mask with pointed ears.

senses.definition: To cover something or make it harder to notice.
senses.example: The sound of rain masked the footsteps outside.

senses.definition: A measure of how much matter something contains or how hard it is to change its motion.
senses.example: A full wagon has more mass than the same empty wagon.

senses.definition: Very large, heavy, or strong.
senses.example: A massive stone stood at the entrance to the cave.

senses.definition: Someone very skilled at doing something.
senses.example: Our guide was a master at telling stories.

senses.definition: To learn to do something very well.
senses.example: It took many tries to master the first song on my recorder.

senses.definition: A work of art or other thing made with outstanding skill.
senses.example: The huge quilt was the artist’s masterpiece.

senses.definition: A contest in a sport or game between people or teams.
senses.example: The tennis match lasted three sets.

senses.definition: To look like or go well with something else.
senses.example: The two blue socks match.

senses.definition: A small stick that can be rubbed on a rough surface to make a flame.
senses.example: An adult used a match to light the candle.

senses.definition: A partner, companion, or the other thing that makes a pair.
senses.example: I found one glove but could not find its mate.

senses.definition: For animals to join together in a way that can produce young.
senses.example: The birds usually mate in spring.

senses.definition: A substance used to make something.
senses.example: The coat is made from a material that keeps out rain.

senses.definition: Information, ideas, or supplies used for a certain activity.
senses.example: We gathered material for our class report.

senses.definition: A subject, question, or problem people are thinking about.
senses.example: The club will discuss the matter at its next meeting.

senses.definition: To be important or make a difference.
senses.example: It matters which trail we take if we want to reach the lake.

senses.definition: The material that makes up things that take up space and have mass.
senses.example: Air is a kind of matter even though you usually cannot see it.

senses.definition: A place or puzzle with many connected paths and a route you have to find.
senses.example: We followed the clues to get out of the corn maze.

senses.definition: An open area of land covered mainly with grass and often with wildflowers.
senses.example: Bees crossed the sunny meadow to reach the flowers.

senses.definition: An average found by adding numbers and dividing the total by how many numbers you added.
senses.example: The mean of three, six, and nine is six.

senses.definition: During the same time that something else is happening.
senses.example: I washed the paint cups. Meanwhile, Tessa cleaned the table.

senses.definition: To find the length, amount, or size of something using an agreed unit.
senses.example: We measured the table to see if it would fit.

senses.definition: A step taken to bring about a result or prevent a problem.
senses.example: The new crosswalk was one measure to make it safer to walk to school.

senses.definition: A pencil that moves a slim stick of writing material toward its point so it can keep writing without being sharpened.
senses.example: Lena clicked her mechanical pencil to bring out more of the writing stick.

senses.definition: A piece of metal, often on a ribbon, given as a sign of honor or for doing well.
senses.example: We cheered when Mina was handed her swimming medal.

senses.definition: The middle value in an ordered list, or the value halfway between the two middle numbers when there are two.
senses.example: After sorting two, five, and twelve, the median is five.

senses.definition: Something used to stop, ease, or prevent an illness.
senses.example: The nurse gave me the medicine my doctor had prescribed.

senses.definition: The work of studying, treating, and preventing illness.
senses.example: Her interest in medicine began with a book about how the body works.

senses.definition: In the middle between two sizes, amounts, or strengths.
senses.example: I needed the medium brush to paint the roof.

senses.definition: A material, method, or tool used to express an idea or send a message.
senses.example: Clay was the medium she chose for the sculpture.

senses.definition: To come together with someone, whether you planned it or not. It can also mean being introduced for the first time.
senses.example: I met my new neighbor at the playground.

senses.definition: To touch or join at a place.
senses.example: The two paths meet near the bridge.

senses.definition: The line of notes that makes the main tune of a piece of music.
senses.example: I hummed the melody of the last song.

senses.definition: The temperature at which a solid begins to change into a liquid under certain conditions.
senses.example: At normal air pressure, ice has a melting point of zero degrees Celsius.

senses.definition: A person or thing that belongs to a group.
senses.example: Each member of the club took a turn explaining a rule.

senses.definition: The ability to remember what you learned or what happened.
senses.example: Nao has a good memory for people’s names.

senses.definition: Something from the past that you remember.
senses.example: Building a kite with Grandpa is a happy memory.

senses.definition: To repair something broken or torn.
senses.example: We mended a rip in the flag before hanging it up.

senses.definition: To heal or get better after being hurt.
senses.example: His wrist began to mend after it was set in a cast.

senses.definition: To speak or write briefly about something.
senses.example: Did you mention the book sale in your note?

senses.definition: A brief statement about something.
senses.example: The sign gave no mention of where to park.

senses.definition: A list of foods and drinks you can order or will be served.
senses.example: The lunch menu listed tomato soup.

senses.definition: A list of choices or actions on a screen.
senses.example: Choose “Print” from the menu.

senses.definition: Only, or nothing more than what is said.
senses.example: The rattle was merely a loose button in the drawer.

senses.definition: Happy and full of good spirits.
senses.example: A merry tune played while we put up the decorations.

senses.definition: A dirty or untidy condition or group of things.
senses.example: We cleaned the mess of scraps left on the floor.

senses.definition: A confusing or difficult situation.
senses.example: The missing bus tickets put us in a mess.

senses.definition: Words or signs sent to tell someone something.
senses.example: Cara left a message saying she found my hat.

senses.definition: To send a written note to someone electronically.
senses.example: I messaged my dad when practice ended.

senses.definition: Information that describes a file or other piece of information.
senses.example: A photo’s metadata can describe when the picture was made.

senses.definition: A material like iron or copper, often strong, shiny, and good at carrying heat or electricity.
senses.example: The spoon is made of shiny metal.

senses.definition: Rock changed from an older rock by heat, pressure, or other changes inside Earth, without melting completely.
senses.example: Marble is a metamorphic rock that can form from limestone.

senses.definition: A comparison that talks about one thing as though it were something else.
senses.example: Calling the moon a silver coin is a metaphor.

senses.definition: A streak of light made when a small object speeds through a planet’s atmosphere.
senses.example: We saw a bright meteor streak across the night sky.

senses.definition: A piece of rock or metal from space that reaches the ground after traveling through an atmosphere.
senses.example: The museum showed a meteorite that landed in a farmer’s field.

senses.definition: A gas that contains carbon and hydrogen. In cold places such as Titan it can form liquid lakes.
senses.example: Scientists found lakes of liquid methane on Titan.

senses.definition: A system of measurements with units such as the meter, liter, and gram, related by powers of ten.
senses.example: In the metric system, a meter is one hundred centimeters.

senses.definition: A condition in which objects act as if there is very little gravity pulling them against their surroundings.
senses.example: In microgravity, an astronaut can let go of a pencil and watch it float.

senses.definition: The part near the center or halfway between two ends.
senses.example: We put the bowl in the middle of the table.

senses.definition: Nearest to the center or halfway between the ends.
senses.example: I stood on the middle step to tie my shoes.

senses.definition: Very strong, powerful, or large.
senses.example: The mighty river carried the raft downstream.

senses.definition: Gentle or moderate in strength, taste, or weather.
senses.example: We chose mild salsa that made our tongues tingle only a little.

senses.definition: A unit for measuring distance equal to 5,280 feet, used in places including the U.S.
senses.example: The trail follows the shore for one mile.

senses.definition: The number 1,000,000, equal to one thousand groups of one thousand.
senses.example: A million pennies would fill much more than a jar.

senses.definition: To copy how someone or something sounds, moves, or looks.
senses.example: The parrot mimicked the sound of a ringing phone.

senses.definition: A person or animal that is good at copying others.
senses.example: Our class mimic could sound just like the school bell.

senses.definition: The part of a person that thinks, remembers, and feels.
senses.example: The puzzle kept my mind busy during the long ride.

senses.definition: To dislike or object to something.
senses.example: Would you mind if I opened the window?

senses.definition: To watch over or look after someone or something.
senses.example: Aunt Noor minded the baby while we made lunch.

senses.definition: Paying attention to something so you remember it or act carefully around it.
senses.example: Please be mindful of the wet paint as you go past the sign.

senses.definition: A solid material that forms in nature and has its own chemical makeup and a regular pattern inside.
senses.example: Quartz is one mineral found in granite.

senses.definition: A substance such as calcium or iron that living things need in small amounts.
senses.example: Calcium is a mineral your body uses to build strong bones.

senses.definition: A small fish. Many kinds of minnows live in fresh water.
senses.example: A group of minnows darted past the reeds.

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.
senses.example: The timer rang one minute after we started the race.

senses.definition: A short time, not always exactly sixty seconds.
senses.example: I’ll be ready in a minute after I find my coat.

senses.definition: Extremely small.
senses.example: A minute speck of dust showed up on the camera lens.

senses.definition: A smooth surface that reflects an image.
senses.example: I looked in the mirror to check my hat.

senses.definition: To show the same pattern, movement, or appearance as something else.
senses.example: Jo mirrored my movements during the game.

senses.definition: Wrongly or in a way that makes a mistake.
senses.example: If you misspell a word, you have spelled it incorrectly.

senses.definition: Very unhappy or uncomfortable.
senses.example: I felt miserable when my socks were cold and wet.

senses.definition: To put something in the wrong place so you cannot easily find it.
senses.example: I misplaced my gloves and found them under a pile of books.

senses.definition: To fail to hit, catch, or reach something.
senses.example: I waved for the bus but missed it.

senses.definition: To notice that someone or something you like is away and wish they were there.
senses.example: I miss my friends when school is out.

senses.definition: To fail to see, hear, or notice something.
senses.example: We missed the small turnoff on the map.

senses.definition: To fail to understand the main idea or what matters most.
senses.example: If you count every cloud but forget why we watched them, you miss the point.

senses.definition: A cloud of tiny water drops floating in the air, often near the ground.
senses.example: A thin mist hung above the lake.

senses.definition: To cover something with very fine drops of liquid.
senses.example: We misted the dry seedlings with a spray bottle.

senses.definition: Something that is wrong or done incorrectly.
senses.example: The missing number was my only mistake on the page.

senses.definition: To think that one person or thing is another by accident.
senses.example: From far away I mistook a plastic bag for a bird.

senses.definition: Full of fine drops of water in the air.
senses.example: The hills looked gray on the misty morning.

senses.definition: To hear, read, or see something but get the wrong idea about it.
senses.example: I misunderstood the sign and went to the wrong door.

senses.definition: A small cell part that helps make energy from food available for the cell to use.
senses.example: A working muscle cell uses the energy its mitochondria help supply.

senses.definition: A way a cell sorts copies of its chromosomes into two groups before it splits into two cells.
senses.example: Cells use mitosis as fresh skin grows.

senses.definition: To combine different things so they are spread through each other.
senses.example: Mix the blue paint with a little white.

senses.definition: A combination of different things.
senses.example: I packed a mix of raisins and pretzels.

senses.definition: A number written with a whole number and a fraction next to it to show their sum.
senses.example: Two and one half is a mixed number.

senses.definition: Two or more kinds of material together that can still keep their own properties.
senses.example: Trail mix is a mixture of different foods.

senses.definition: A copy of something, often smaller, used to show what it looks like or how it works.
senses.example: Our model of the solar system hung from the ceiling.

senses.definition: A person or thing that others can use as a good example.
senses.example: Her careful notes were a model for the rest of the class.

senses.definition: To build or show a version of something so others can understand or copy it.
senses.example: We modeled a hillside with clay and sticks.

senses.definition: Slightly wet or damp.
senses.example: We kept the soil moist until the seeds began to grow.

senses.definition: A large tooth farther back in the mouth, used to crush and grind food.
senses.example: This molar helps me chew pieces of bread.

senses.definition: A group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
senses.example: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

senses.definition: A very short time or a particular point in time.
senses.example: At that moment the lights came on.

senses.definition: A way to measure motion that depends on an object’s mass, speed, and direction.
senses.example: A fast-moving cart has more momentum than the same cart moving slowly.

senses.definition: The energy or support that keeps an activity or effort going.
senses.example: Our coat drive gained momentum when the first group brought in twenty coats.

senses.definition: A screen that shows pictures or information from a computer or other machine.
senses.example: The map appeared on the larger monitor.

senses.definition: To check how something is doing or changing over time.
senses.example: We monitored the temperature in the room each morning.

senses.definition: A wind pattern that changes direction with the seasons and often brings a rainy season.
senses.example: The summer monsoon brought heavy rain to the fields.

senses.definition: One of the twelve parts of a year, such as January or June.
senses.example: We marked the last day of each month on the calendar.

senses.definition: The way you are feeling, or the feeling a place or story creates.
senses.example: The eager dog put me in a good mood.

senses.definition: A natural object that travels around a planet, dwarf planet, or other small world. We call Earth’s own moon the Moon.
senses.example: Ganymede is a moon of Jupiter.

senses.definition: A ridge or pile of loose material carried and left by a glacier.
senses.example: The rocky moraine showed where the glacier once reached.

senses.definition: The lesson that a story asks you to think about.
senses.example: The moral of the story was that a small friend can still help.

senses.definition: The early part of the day, usually up to noon.
senses.example: We watered the garden in the morning before it got hot.

senses.definition: A picture or pattern made by fitting together many small pieces of stone, tile, glass, or another material.
senses.example: We used paper squares to make a mosaic of a fish.

senses.definition: A slender flying insect. In many kinds, the females can bite people or other animals to take blood.
senses.example: A mosquito buzzed past my ear beside the pond.

senses.definition: More than half of a group, or a very large part of it.
senses.example: Most of the leaves had fallen by Friday.

senses.definition: To the greatest degree.
senses.example: Of all the visits, I enjoyed the one to the train yard most.

senses.definition: For the largest part or most of the time.
senses.example: The basket was mostly full of apples, with a few pears on top.

senses.definition: The act or process of moving.
senses.example: The smooth motion of the swings made Ana sleepy.

senses.definition: To move your hand, head, or body to show what someone should do.
senses.example: The guide motioned for us to follow her.

senses.definition: A reason for doing something.
senses.example: The detective looked for a motive for taking the old painting.

senses.definition: A machine that makes a part move using power from electricity, fuel or another source.
senses.example: An electric motor turned the fan’s blades.

senses.definition: A natural part of the land that rises high above the area around it.
senses.example: We saw the peak of the mountain from the train.

senses.definition: A small animal with sharp front teeth for gnawing, rounded ears, and usually a long tail.
senses.example: A mouse darted through the tall grass.

senses.definition: A small device you move with your hand to steer a pointer on a computer screen. Its buttons let you select things.
senses.example: I moved the mouse to put the pointer on the picture.

senses.definition: The opening of the face used for eating, speaking, and breathing.
senses.example: I covered my mouth when I yawned.

senses.definition: An opening into a place or where a river flows into more open water.
senses.example: The boat crossed the mouth of the river.

senses.definition: To move your lips as if saying words without using your voice.
senses.example: Rae mouthed the answer so she would not interrupt the song.

senses.definition: To change where something is or go somewhere else.
senses.example: We moved the chairs into a circle.

senses.definition: To go to live in a different place.
senses.example: My friend moved to another town last spring.

senses.definition: One action or turn in a game, dance, or plan.
senses.example: Moving the knight was my first move.

senses.definition: Wet earth, usually soft enough to stick or leave tracks.
senses.example: Our boots sank in the mud near the gate.

senses.definition: Covered with mud or mixed with mud.
senses.example: Mud from the path left my boots muddy.

senses.definition: A small baked bread or cake often made in a round cup-shaped pan.
senses.example: I saved a blueberry muffin for my sister.

senses.definition: A covering such as straw or wood chips laid over soil to help hold water or limit weeds.
senses.example: The mulch shaded the soil around the plants.

senses.definition: A number made by multiplying a given number by a whole number.
senses.example: Twelve is a multiple of three.

senses.definition: In arithmetic, to find a product, such as the total in equal groups. Multiplying three by four gives twelve.
senses.example: We multiplied the number of rows by the number of seats in each row.

senses.definition: To become or make more numerous.
senses.example: The scratches on the old table multiplied over the years.
